audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Deuteronomy / Devarim debt-release, poverty, servant-release, and firstborn law, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for seventh-year release, lending ethics, poverty contradiction, open-hand command, anti-hardheartedness warning, Hebrew servant liberation gifts, voluntary permanent service, and firstborn animal consecration.

verses.restored: At end of seven years you shall make a release.

familiar.text: At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release.

modern.text: At the end of every seven years you must cancel debts.

original.text: מִקֵּ֥ץ שֶֽׁבַע שָׁנִ֖ים תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה שְׁמִטָּֽה

verses.restored: This is matter of release: every creditor shall release what he lent to his neighbor; he shall not press his neighbor or his brother, because release to YHWH has been proclaimed.

familiar.text: And this is the manner of the release: Every creditor that lendeth ought unto his neighbour shall release it; he shall not exact it of his neighbour, or of his brother; because it is called the LORD’s release.

modern.text: This is the manner of remission: Every creditor shall cancel what he has loaned to his neighbor. He is not to collect anything from his neighbor or brother, because the LORD’s time of release has been proclaimed.

original.text: וְזֶה֮ דְּבַ֣ר הַשְּׁמִטָּה֒ שָׁמ֗וֹט כָּל בַּ֨עַל֙ מַשֵּׁ֣ה יָד֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַשֶּׁ֖ה בְּרֵעֵ֑הוּ לֹֽא יִגֹּ֤שׂ אֶת רֵעֵ֨הוּ֙ וְאֶת אָחִ֔יו כִּֽי קָרָ֥א שְׁמִטָּ֖ה לַֽיהוָֽה

verses.restored: The foreigner you may press, but what is yours with your brother your hand shall release.

familiar.text: Of a foreigner thou mayest exact it again: but that which is thine with thy brother thine hand shall release;

modern.text: You may collect something from a foreigner, but you must forgive whatever your brother owes you.

original.text: אֶת הַנָּכְרִ֖י תִּגֹּ֑שׂ וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ אֶת אָחִ֖יךָ תַּשְׁמֵ֥ט יָדֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Yet there should be no poor among you, for YHWH will surely bless you in land YHWH your Divine gives you as inheritance to possess,

familiar.text: Save when there shall be no poor among you; for the LORD shall greatly bless thee in the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee for an inheritance to possess it:

modern.text: There will be no poor among you, however, because the LORD will surely bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess as an inheritance,

original.text: אֶ֕פֶס כִּ֛י לֹ֥א יִֽהְיֶה בְּךָ֖ אֶבְי֑וֹן כִּֽי בָרֵ֤ךְ יְבָֽרֶכְךָ֙ יְהוָ֔ה בָּאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ נֹֽתֵן לְךָ֥ נַחֲלָ֖ה לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ

verses.restored: if only you diligently listen to voice of YHWH your Divine, keeping to do all this command I command you today.

familiar.text: Only if thou carefully hearken unto the voice of the LORD thy God, to observe to do all these commandments which I command thee this day.

modern.text: if only you obey the LORD your God and are careful to follow all these commandments I am giving you today.

original.text: רַ֚ק אִם שָׁמ֣וֹעַ תִּשְׁמַ֔ע בְּק֖וֹל יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לִשְׁמֹ֤ר לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ אֶת כָּל הַמִּצְוָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁ֛ר אָנֹכִ֥י מְצַוְּךָ֖ הַיּֽוֹם

verses.restored: For YHWH your Divine will bless you as he spoke to you; you shall lend to many nations but shall not borrow, and rule over many nations but they shall not rule over you.

familiar.text: For the LORD thy God blesseth thee, as he promised thee: and thou shalt lend unto many nations, but thou shalt not borrow; and thou shalt reign over many nations, but they shall not reign over thee.

modern.text: When the LORD your God blesses you as He has promised, you will lend to many nations but borrow from none; you will rule over many nations but be ruled by none. Generosity in Lending and Giving (Matthew 6:1–4)

original.text: כִּֽי יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ בֵּֽרַכְךָ֔ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּר לָ֑ךְ וְהַֽעֲבַטְתָּ֞ גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֗ים וְאַתָּה֙ לֹ֣א תַעֲבֹ֔ט וּמָֽשַׁלְתָּ֙ בְּגוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֔ים וּבְךָ֖ לֹ֥א יִמְשֹֽׁלוּ

verses.restored: If there is among you a poor person, one of your brothers, within one of your gates in your land YHWH your Divine gives you, you shall not harden your heart or shut your hand from your poor brother.

familiar.text: If there be among you a poor man of one of thy brethren within any of thy gates in thy land which the LORD thy God giveth thee, thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother:

modern.text: If there is a poor man among your brothers within any of the gates in the land that the LORD your God is giving you, then you are not to harden your heart or shut your hand from your poor brother.

original.text: כִּֽי יִהְיֶה֩ בְךָ֨ אֶבְי֜וֹן מֵאַחַ֤ד אַחֶ֨יךָ֙ בְּאַחַ֣ד שְׁעָרֶ֔יךָ בְּאַ֨רְצְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֣ן לָ֑ךְ לֹ֧א תְאַמֵּ֣ץ אֶת לְבָבְךָ֗ וְלֹ֤א תִקְפֹּץ֙ אֶת יָ֣דְךָ֔ מֵאָחִ֖יךָ הָאֶבְיֽוֹן

verses.restored: But you shall surely open your hand to him and surely lend him enough for his lack, whatever is lacking to him.

familiar.text: But thou shalt open thine hand wide unto him, and shalt surely lend him sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth.

modern.text: Instead, you are to open your hand to him and freely loan him whatever he needs.

original.text: כִּֽי פָתֹ֧חַ תִּפְתַּ֛ח אֶת יָדְךָ֖ ל֑וֹ וְהַעֲבֵט֙ תַּעֲבִיטֶ֔נּוּ דֵּ֚י מַחְסֹר֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֶחְסַ֖ר לֽוֹ

verses.restored: Guard yourself lest there be a worthless word in your heart, saying, Seventh year, year of release, is near, and your eye is evil toward your poor brother and you give him nothing; he may cry to YHWH against you, and sin/misalignment will be in you.

familiar.text: Beware that there be not a thought in thy wicked heart, saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand; and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother, and thou givest him nought; and he cry unto the LORD against thee, and it be sin unto thee.

modern.text: Be careful not to harbor this wicked thought in your heart: “The seventh year, the year of release, is near,” so that you look upon your poor brother begrudgingly and give him nothing. He will cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.

original.text: הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֡ פֶּן יִהְיֶ֣ה דָבָר֩ עִם לְבָבְךָ֨ בְלִיַּ֜עַל לֵאמֹ֗ר קָֽרְבָ֣ה שְׁנַֽת הַשֶּׁבַע֮ שְׁנַ֣ת הַשְּׁמִטָּה֒ וְרָעָ֣ה עֵֽינְךָ֗ בְּאָחִ֨יךָ֙ הָֽאֶבְי֔וֹן וְלֹ֥א תִתֵּ֖ן ל֑וֹ וְקָרָ֤א עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶל יְהוָ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה בְךָ֖ חֵֽטְא

verses.restored: You shall surely give to him, and your heart shall not be grieved when you give, because for this thing YHWH your Divine will bless you in all your work and in all undertaking of your hand.

familiar.text: Thou shalt surely give him, and thine heart shall not be grieved when thou givest unto him: because that for this thing the LORD thy God shall bless thee in all thy works, and in all that thou puttest thine hand unto.

modern.text: Give generously to him, and do not let your heart be grieved when you do so. And because of this the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in everything to which you put your hand.

original.text: נָת֤וֹן תִּתֵּן֙ ל֔וֹ וְלֹא יֵרַ֥ע לְבָבְךָ֖ בְּתִתְּךָ֣ ל֑וֹ כִּ֞י בִּגְלַ֣ל הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה יְבָרֶכְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכָֽל מַעֲשֶׂ֔ךָ וּבְכֹ֖ל מִשְׁלַ֥ח יָדֶֽךָ

verses.restored: For poor will not cease from midst of land; therefore I command you, saying, You shall surely open your hand to your brother, to your poor and needy in your land.

familiar.text: For the poor shall never cease out of the land: therefore I command thee, saying, Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy, in thy land.

modern.text: For there will never cease to be poor in the land; that is why I am commanding you to open wide your hand to your brother and to the poor and needy in your land. Hebrew Servants (Exodus 21:1–11)

original.text: כִּ֛י לֹא יֶחְדַּ֥ל אֶבְי֖וֹן מִקֶּ֣רֶב הָאָ֑רֶץ עַל כֵּ֞ן אָנֹכִ֤י מְצַוְּךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר פָּ֠תֹחַ תִּפְתַּ֨ח אֶת יָדְךָ֜ לְאָחִ֧יךָ לַעֲנִיֶּ֛ךָ וּלְאֶבְיֹנְךָ֖ בְּאַרְצֶֽךָ

verses.restored: If your brother, a Hebrew man or Hebrew woman, is sold to you, he shall serve you six years, and in seventh year you shall send him free from you.

familiar.text: And if thy brother, an Hebrew man, or an Hebrew woman, be sold unto thee, and serve thee six years; then in the seventh year thou shalt let him go free from thee.

modern.text: If a fellow Hebrew, a man or a woman, is sold to you and serves you six years, then in the seventh year you must set him free.

original.text: כִּֽי יִמָּכֵ֨ר לְךָ֜ אָחִ֣יךָ הָֽעִבְרִ֗י א֚וֹ הָֽעִבְרִיָּ֔ה וַעֲבָֽדְךָ֖ שֵׁ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֑ים וּבַשָּׁנָה֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔ת תְּשַׁלְּחֶ֥נּוּ חָפְשִׁ֖י מֵעִמָּֽךְ

verses.restored: When you send him free from you, you shall not send him empty.

familiar.text: And when thou sendest him out free from thee, thou shalt not let him go away empty:

modern.text: And when you release him, do not send him away empty-handed.

original.text: וְכִֽי תְשַׁלְּחֶ֥נּוּ חָפְשִׁ֖י מֵֽעִמָּ֑ךְ לֹ֥א תְשַׁלְּחֶ֖נּוּ רֵיקָֽם

verses.restored: You shall surely furnish him from your flock, threshing floor, and winepress; from what YHWH your Divine blessed you, you shall give to him.

familiar.text: Thou shalt furnish him liberally out of thy flock, and out of thy floor, and out of thy winepress: of that wherewith the LORD thy God hath blessed thee thou shalt give unto him.

modern.text: You are to furnish him liberally from your flock, your threshing floor, and your winepress. You shall give to him as the LORD your God has blessed you.

original.text: הַעֲנֵ֤יק תַּעֲנִיק֙ ל֔וֹ מִצֹּ֣אנְךָ֔ וּמִֽגָּרְנְךָ֖ וּמִיִּקְבֶ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֧ר בֵּרַכְךָ֛ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ תִּתֶּן לֽוֹ

verses.restored: You shall remember you were a slave in land of Egypt and YHWH your Divine redeemed you; therefore I command you this thing today.

familiar.text: And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt, and the LORD thy God redeemed thee: therefore I command thee this thing to day.

modern.text: Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you; that is why I am giving you this command today.

original.text: וְזָכַרְתָּ֗ כִּ֣י עֶ֤בֶד הָיִ֨יתָ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַֽיִּפְדְּךָ֖ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ עַל כֵּ֞ן אָנֹכִ֧י מְצַוְּךָ֛ אֶת הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה הַיּֽוֹם

verses.restored: It shall be, if he says to you, I will not go out from you, because he loves you and your house, because it is good for him with you,

familiar.text: And it shall be, if he say unto thee, I will not go away from thee; because he loveth thee and thine house, because he is well with thee;

modern.text: But if your servant says to you, ‘I do not want to leave you,’ because he loves you and your household and is well off with you,

original.text: וְהָיָה֙ כִּֽי יֹאמַ֣ר אֵלֶ֔יךָ לֹ֥א אֵצֵ֖א מֵעִמָּ֑ךְ כִּ֤י אֲהֵֽבְךָ֙ וְאֶת בֵּיתֶ֔ךָ כִּי ט֥וֹב ל֖וֹ עִמָּֽךְ

verses.restored: then you shall take awl and put it through his ear into door, and he shall be your servant permanently; and also to your female servant you shall do likewise.

familiar.text: Then thou shalt take an aul, and thrust it through his ear unto the door, and he shall be thy servant for ever. And also unto thy maidservant thou shalt do likewise.

modern.text: then take an awl and pierce it through his ear into the door, and he will become your servant for life. And treat your maidservant the same way.

original.text: וְלָקַחְתָּ֣ אֶת הַמַּרְצֵ֗עַ וְנָתַתָּ֤ה בְאָזְנוֹ֙ וּבַדֶּ֔לֶת וְהָיָ֥ה לְךָ֖ עֶ֣בֶד עוֹלָ֑ם וְאַ֥ף לַאֲמָתְךָ֖ תַּעֲשֶׂה כֵּֽן

verses.restored: It shall not be hard in your eyes when you send him free from you, for double value of hired worker he served you six years; and YHWH your Divine will bless you in all you do.

familiar.text: It shall not seem hard unto thee, when thou sendest him away free from thee; for he hath been worth a double hired servant to thee, in serving thee six years: and the LORD thy God shall bless thee in all that thou doest.

modern.text: Do not regard it as a hardship to set your servant free, because his six years of service were worth twice the wages of a hired hand. And the LORD your God will bless you in all you do. Firstborn Animals (Exodus 13:1–16)

original.text: לֹא יִקְשֶׁ֣ה בְעֵינֶ֗ךָ בְּשַׁלֵּֽחֲךָ֙ אֹת֤וֹ חָפְשִׁי֙ מֵֽעִמָּ֔ךְ כִּ֗י מִשְׁנֶה֙ שְׂכַ֣ר שָׂכִ֔יר עֲבָֽדְךָ֖ שֵׁ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֑ים וּבֵֽרַכְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֶֽׂה

verses.restored: Every firstborn male born in your herd and flock you shall sanctify to YHWH your Divine; you shall not work with firstborn of ox or shear firstborn of flock.

familiar.text: All the firstling males that come of thy herd and of thy flock thou shalt sanctify unto the LORD thy God: thou shalt do no work with the firstling of thy bullock, nor shear the firstling of thy sheep.

modern.text: You must set apart to the LORD your God every firstborn male produced by your herds and flocks. You are not to put the firstborn of your oxen to work, nor are you to shear the firstborn of your flock.

original.text: כָּֽל הַבְּכ֡וֹר אֲשֶׁר֩ יִוָּלֵ֨ד בִּבְקָרְךָ֤ וּבְצֹֽאנְךָ֙ הַזָּכָ֔ר תַּקְדִּ֖ישׁ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לֹ֤א תַעֲבֹד֙ בִּבְכֹ֣ר שׁוֹרֶ֔ךָ וְלֹ֥א תָגֹ֖ז בְּכ֥וֹר צֹאנֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Before YHWH your Divine you shall eat it year by year in place YHWH chooses, you and your household.

familiar.text: Thou shalt eat it before the LORD thy God year by year in the place which the LORD shall choose, thou and thy household.

modern.text: Each year you and your household are to eat it before the LORD your God in the place the LORD will choose.

original.text: לִפְנֵי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֤יךָ תֹאכֲלֶ֨נּוּ֙ שָׁנָ֣ה בְשָׁנָ֔ה בַּמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה אַתָּ֖ה וּבֵיתֶֽךָ

verses.restored: If there is in it blemish—lame or blind, any bad blemish—you shall not sacrifice it to YHWH your Divine.

familiar.text: And if there be any blemish therein, as if it be lame, or blind, or have any ill blemish, thou shalt not sacrifice it unto the LORD thy God.

modern.text: But if an animal has a defect, is lame or blind, or has any serious flaw, you must not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.

original.text: וְכִֽי יִהְיֶ֨ה ב֜וֹ מ֗וּם פִּסֵּ֨חַ֙ א֣וֹ עִוֵּ֔ר כֹּ֖ל מ֣וּם רָ֑ע לֹ֣א תִזְבָּחֶ֔נּוּ לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: Within your gates you shall eat it; unclean and clean together, like gazelle and deer.

familiar.text: Thou shalt eat it within thy gates: the unclean and the clean person shall eat it alike, as the roebuck, and as the hart.

modern.text: Eat it within your gates; both the ceremonially unclean and clean may eat it as they would a gazelle or a deer.

original.text: בִּשְׁעָרֶ֖יךָ תֹּאכֲלֶ֑נּוּ הַטָּמֵ֤א וְהַטָּהוֹר֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו כַּצְּבִ֖י וְכָאַיָּֽל

verses.restored: Only its blood you shall not eat; upon earth you shall pour it like water.

familiar.text: Only thou shalt not eat the blood thereof; thou shalt pour it upon the ground as water.

modern.text: But you must not eat the blood; pour it on the ground like water.

original.text: רַ֥ק אֶת דָּמ֖וֹ לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֑ל עַל הָאָ֥רֶץ תִּשְׁפְּכֶ֖נּוּ כַּמָּֽיִם

translation_notes: The seventh-year release interrupts indefinite debt pressure within the covenant community.
Verse 4's vision that there need be no poor stands beside verse 11's realism that poverty persists; the tension intensifies rather than cancels the open-hand command.
The permission to press a foreigner reflects unequal ancient in-group/out-group economics and must not justify predatory lending or xenophobia.
The poor person's actual lack determines the response; giving is not limited to symbolic charity.
Hebrew servants, male and female, are released with productive assets because Exodus memory forbids liberation into destitution.
Permanent ear-piercing service remains an ancient dependency structure and must not be romanticized as consent free from economic pressure.
Disability language about sacrificial blemish concerns altar eligibility, not the worth of disabled humans or animals.
safety_note: Do not use Deuteronomy 15 to defend slavery, debt bondage, xenophobic finance, coerced service, or disability stigma. Center debt release, open-handed provision, liberation with resources, and the Exodus demand that freedom must be materially survivable.
